A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ICoT/ADS research. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures and v2 supplementary material support comparison; relocated material can be matched.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark results, ADS/FVI ablations, KV-cache and demonstration comparisons, patch-count sensitivity results and qualitative cases.

after.justification: V2 reports revised benchmark and ablation results, retains the supplementary analyses, and adds original captioning and VQA results in Table 5.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 replace the signal membership test with equality and remove the unused Indices return from ADS and its caller. These are limited pseudocode/interface revisions; Top-K selection, spatial reordering and interleaved generation remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Supplementary Section 9 adds Flickr30k captioning and OKVQA evaluation, extending coverage beyond the retained M3CoT, ScienceQA and LLaVA-W experiments. This is a limited extension evaluated with one-shot Chameleon.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains No-CoT, Multimodal CoT, CCoT, DDCoT and SCAFFOLD for both backbones. New Table 5 compares ICoT with unaugmented Chameleon, rather than introducing another comparison method.

E3.justification: Table 5 introduces one-shot Chameleon evaluation using CIDEr and VQA accuracy. Section 4.5 also revises the reported ablation control: v1 equates joint ADS/FVI removal with plain multimodal CoT, while v2 specifies random demonstration patches for w/o FVI. The main benchmark settings remain stated the same; score revisions alone do not establish protocol changes or reruns.

E4.justification: The documented FVI ablation is revised from the normal-demonstration/plain-CoT removal account to an explicit random-patch control. This changes how its evidence should be interpreted without establishing when the implementation changed. KV-cache, demonstration-source and error-case analyses remain; the patch-count study and Figure 4 are relocated to Supplementary Section 8.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Parenthesized ablation values remain performance differences, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 substantially revise M3CoT and ScienceQA results while retaining LLaVA-W scores. In Table 1, one-shot Chameleon ICoT on M3CoT changes from 33.6 to 32.3, with its reported relative lead falling from 8.0% to 2.8%; one-shot Qwen2-VL ICoT on ScienceQA changes from 54.4 to 65.4. New Table 5 reports Chameleon versus ICoT scores of 22.3 versus 23.6 CIDEr and 26.2 versus 28.2 VQA accuracy. The main score revisions are not explained.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and Equations 1–6 retain their meaning. Equation 5 changes token indexing notation to fv[i]; no new assumptions, theoretical results, derivations or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the claims of image-interleaved reasoning, training-free ADS, applicability to two VLM architectures, improved interpretability and gains up to 14%.

C2.justification: The conclusion newly acknowledges memory overhead from storing attention scores and adds grounding methods as a possible future remedy. The fixed-patch-count limitation is retained. Supplementary Section 9 additionally discusses applicability to tasks requiring less reasoning.

D1.justification: V2 adds a first-page code-repository pointer, an illustrative one-shot FVI demonstration in Figure 5, and explicit stopping conditions of maximum generation length or an end-of-sequence token. These improve documentation without establishing changes to the underlying implementation.

R1.justification: The same 34 references and positioning against text-only multimodal CoT are retained. Correcting the order of the backbone architecture descriptions does not change the research positioning.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized grammatical and terminology corrections, revises the ablation and limitations paragraphs, reformats author information, adds acknowledgements, and organizes supplementary Sections 8–10. Most of the narrative remains unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 adds Table 5 and the demonstration in Figure 5, moves the existing Figure 4 to the supplement, and adjusts the author block and surrounding pagination. Existing main figures and table structures are retained; numerical replacements are assessed under E6.

improvement.justification: V2 modestly improves reproducibility and transparency through the repository pointer, stopping-rule explanation, more explicit ablation controls and attention-memory limitation, while adding limited captioning/VQA evidence. These benefits are tempered by unexplained broad score revisions and Figure 5 calling option C incorrect before concluding that it is correct. The additions support a limited overall improvement, not a substantial strengthening of the central scientific evidence.
